body:
GridMap does a deferred octant sync and the debug requires the Node to be in the world and tree to access both rendering scenario RID (so you can see stuff) and transforms (so it can place stuff), else the setup runs void.

The real "bug" here is the existence of the `change_scene_xyz` methods together with the `SceneTree::process()` that does the actual change.

Both are pure code-rot full of hacks. Those methods spawn the new object but then wait with the scene change for the SceneTree process function and only after a double "little-hack" with the MessageQueue flush they update and cause their own scene change and add the child node, all in the middle of the "locked" process.

So basically every single class and object that does deferred setups has a random chance of breaking just by order of luck how the queues get flushed. That is why those `change_scene_xyz` methods collect and cause so many bugs.
